# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Pick the channel by the receiver, not by habit. A message sent in a sense they
  lack is not a message; it is a turn spent talking to the room.

- Exactly one of you can read the signs and still speak. Their spoken lines are
  the answer's only road to the hands, so spend them well.

- Agree on a small code before trading facts. A code invented mid-stream settles
  nothing, and one set first makes every later message cheap.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
BUTTON [large] [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[green] 3:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌ 👍 🤟]

The bomb shows display `0`, a green light, a large button labeled “PUSH TO DEFUSE,” and three wires: red, green, yellow. I am sending these observations in speech so Mute can apply the manual and relay the required procedure to Blind. I also acknowledge the gesture sequence, but its meaning is not established to me.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="I see display 0. The light is green. There is one large button labeled PUSH TO DEFUSE. Wires are 1 red, 2 green, 3 yellow. Please use the manual and tell Blind exactly what to do.")
speak(to="blind", text="I see display 0, a green light, one large PUSH TO DEFUSE button, and wires 1 red, 2 green, 3 yellow. Wait for Mute's manual-based instructions.")
wait()
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
BUTTON [large] [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[green] 3:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 ☝ 👎 🖐]

The bomb’s visible state is unchanged. Mute has sent four gestures to me: thumbs up, pointing up, thumbs down, and an open hand. No code for these gestures has been established, so I should relay their literal descriptions to Blind while asking Mute to provide the manual’s instructions by speech.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Mute signaled me four gestures: thumbs up, pointing up, thumbs down, open hand. No gesture code has been established, so do not treat them as instructions. The bomb remains display 0, green light, large PUSH TO DEFUSE button, wires 1 red, 2 green, 3 yellow.")
speak(to="mute", text="Please speak the manual's exact instructions to Blind; gestures have no agreed code.")
wait()
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
BUTTON [large] [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[green] 3:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎 ☝ 🤞]

The bomb remains unchanged. Mute’s new gestures are thumbs down, pointing up, and crossed fingers, but no gesture code has been agreed, so I cannot safely interpret them. The reliable route is for Mute to read the manual and speak its exact instructions directly to Blind. I will repeat the bomb state and warn Blind not to act on unverified gestures.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="The bomb is unchanged: display 0, green light, large PUSH TO DEFUSE button, wires 1 red, 2 green, 3 yellow. Please read the manual and speak the exact required action to Blind.")
speak(to="blind", text="The bomb remains display 0, green light, large PUSH TO DEFUSE button, wires 1 red, 2 green, 3 yellow. Mute's gestures are not an agreed code; wait for Mute's spoken manual instructions.")
wait()
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
BUTTON [large] [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[green] 3:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎 ☝ 🤞]

The bomb is still unchanged. Mute cannot speak, so the manual’s answer must come through a defined gesture code, after which I can speak the decoded instruction to Blind. I am establishing a compact action code: thumbs up means press the button; the three numbered hand signs mean cut wires 1–3; open hand means wait. I will ask Mute to resend the manual’s required action using that code.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="New code for your manual answer: 👍 means press the button; ☝ means cut wire 1; ✌ means cut wire 2; 🤟 means cut wire 3; 🖐 means wait. Send the required action using these gestures, and send multiple gestures in order if needed.")
speak(to="blind", text="Mute cannot speak. I have established an action code and am waiting for the manual's decoded instruction. Do not act yet.")
wait()
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
BUTTON [large] [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[green] 3:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝]

The bomb remains unchanged. Under the code I established, Mute’s single ☝ means the manual requires cutting wire 1. I am relaying that exact action to Blind; no button press or other wire action is indicated.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="The manual instruction received from Mute is: cut wire 1, the red wire. Do not press the button or cut another wire.")
wait()
```
